RE-MEASURED HOURS LATER, ON THE SAME DESIGN, AFTER THE COST IT NAMED WAS FIXED. Its SAVE column is no longer current:

    build export doc   1,137.3 ms -> 236.5 ms
    TOTAL session save 1,168.3 ms -> 265.3 ms

WHICH PART MOVED, precisely — this is a PARTIAL supersession and the node is NOT closed: only the write side. Its load figures still stand within noise (1,098 ms then, 1,156 ms after; the ~8% import regression from BTreeMap inserts is inside that). Its two headline findings BOTH survive and one is strengthened: the full-text index is cheap and derived, and the byte store is not the bottleneck — the remaining save cost is not storage either.

⭐ AND ITS OWN PREDICTION CAME TRUE. That fact called out `build_export_doc` at 1,137 ms as "the dominant cost moved to a place nobody has looked... the same SHAPE as the import defect just fixed... very likely another `Vec` somewhere." It was a HashMap, and the shape was exactly right: a linear scan standing in for an indexed lookup. The node earned its keep by naming the next measurement, which is what a good measurement does.

🛑 SECOND INSTANCE OF A KNOWN BLIND SPOT, AND IT WAS PREDICTED IN ADVANCE. `unclaimed_findings` on this ChangeEvent returned nothing with subjects_examined=1, exactly as `fact:unclaimed-findings-cannot-join-a-change-to-a-finding-hung-off-a-different-node` said it would: the change is anchored to `cmp:byte-store` (the code) and this observation to a Decision (the question it answered), so the join never happens. Closed by judgement again. A HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT edge from cmp:byte-store has now been drawn so the next change to that component reaches it.
